title: Fix MSVC build: wrap max/min calls to prevent macro expansion by dbwls99706 · Pull Request #3043 · ros2/rclcpp · GitHub
body_rendered_text:
Fixes #2947


Description


Wrap max() and min() calls with parentheses to prevent windows.h macro interference.


Modified files:



simple_events_queue.hpp


events_queue.hpp


utilities.hpp


create_timer.hpp



Is this user-facing behavior change?


No


Did you use Generative AI?


Yes, Claude was used to identify affected files and generate the fix pattern.


Additional Information


This approach is more robust than defining NOMINMAX, as it works regardless of header include order.

I am sorry, but I would reject these changes.

This is clearly a problem of including headers in the wrong order etc on the client side.

I don't see a point of messing up our code base because of this.

i am with @jmachowinski on this.


the root cause is obviously on client side, and this is the user's responsibility. (Downstream packages should either define NOMINMAX globally or ensure proper include ordering.)


this PR is uglier and less idiomatic... 😓 i am not inclined to take this because of above...
Yep, I missed that this had been fixed elsewhere.  Thanks for the second (and third!) look.
That being said, thanks for tackling an open issue @dbwls99706!
